facts.text: Renamed Viola on December 26, 1882—likely in honor of the daughter of the first postmaster, William H.
The Spokane and Inland Empire Railroad arrived in the early 1900s, turning Viola into a passenger station that shipped apples across the Inland Northwest.
Viola Cemetery, founded in 1896 on a hill overlooking the town, holds more than 750 graves of early settlers and veterans.
Viola sits in the Palouse, where rolling loess hills make the land perfect for dryland wheat and legume farming.
Viola has a humid continental climate, with cold winters, warm summers, and most rain falling in fall and winter.
The Viola Community Club, founded in 1923 by the University of Idaho, built a clubhouse in 1948 and now hosts local events.
